clue.text: Preference given to a blonde when it comes to the push?

definitions.text: Preference given to a blonde when it comes to the push?

parts.words: Preference given to a blonde when it comes to the push
parts.note: being sacked (given the push) is called unjust when the fair-haired are kept on and the dark-haired let go, a pun on fair meaning blonde

explanation.surface: A boss favours blondes when deciding whom to keep on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacking that breaks employment rules is the legal term for wrongful firing; here the 'un-fair' are the ones being let go.

clue.text: Spook given lack of space by Holy Writ

parts.note: too little space or reporting given to a story is under-coverage
NT, the New Testament, is part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A ghost complains that scripture leaves it no room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' is slang for a spy, not a ghost; 'given ... by' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is informal for a spy, and a spy working in disguise is an undercover operative.

clue.text: Group of gasteropods force us to repeat

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: the instruction tells us to write the word us twice over

explanation.surface: A zoologist forces us to keep repeating a snail classification.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusus is a genus of spindle-shaped sea snails, a group within the gastropod molluscs.

clue.text: State of train that is broken down

indicators.note: a broken-down train is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged along with the abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A railway report says the train is out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a state of inactivity or sluggishness, the condition of a body at rest.

clue.text: Inferior clergy get a second turn

indicators.note: giving the letters of these two words a turn rearranges them

explanation.surface: Junior churchmen are told to have another go.
explanation.definitionFit: Deacons rank below priests in the clerical orders, hence inferior clergy.

clue.text: There's a little bubble mixture when it fizzes

definitions.text: There's a little bubble mixture when it fizzes

indicators.note: a mixture is a mixing, so these letters are stirred into a new order
just a little of the word bubble, its first letter

explanation.surface: Something gives off a few bubbles as it fizzes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the sweet powder too: a fizzy mixture that produces little bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet effervescent powder that fizzes on the tongue.

clue.text: Near the coast there's said to be cover

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to insure is to give cover, as an insurance policy does

explanation.surface: By the sea, people reckon there is shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech 'insure' and the answer sound much alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore describes waters or fishing close to the shore rather than out at sea.

clue.text: It's barbed when it turns up in a fresh carcass

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the rearranged letters
a fresh version of the word carcass is a new arrangement of its letters
in a down clue the word it reads upwards

explanation.surface: Something spiky is found when it appears inside a newly killed body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's barbed' tempts as the definition, but 'it' is fodder; only 'barbed' defines, and in a down clue 'turns up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed remark is cutting and pointed, which is what a mocking, sneering remark is.

clue.text: Raise the fence to enable communication?

parts.note: to raise is to lift
taken as written
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hoist a garden fence to let neighbours chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' is the criminal sense, a dealer in stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking up the telephone handset is what you do in order to talk to someone on the line.

clue.text: Mad speed — speed that's utterly reckless

indicators.note: something mad is crazed, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: speed means rate, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A driver going at wild speed is called totally irresponsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the first 'speed' is fodder as written and the second is RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate can mean having no regard for danger, so it describes wildly rash behaviour.

clue.text: Property of some types backfires

indicators.note: back tells us the word fires runs from end to start

parts.note: the word fires is the tail of backfires, so its letters sit there by coincidence of the split: back is read as the signal and fires as the fodder

explanation.surface: A characteristic of certain models is that they go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backfires' is split as BACK (the reversal signal) plus FIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke on letters in certain typefaces, a feature of some fonts.

clue.text: Drunk and disorderly riot over a dish

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A drunken brawl breaks out over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk and disorderly' reads as the police charge, but 'disorderly' rearranges SOT and RIOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Lad said worker is unlikely to go under

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, giving its sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker

explanation.surface: A young man says his labourer will never sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant means able to float, so it is not likely to sink beneath the water.

clue.text: Female born to endless necessity

indicators.note: without its end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a need is a necessity

explanation.surface: A woman is born into dire want.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, marks a married woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Shop ran out, owing to demise of producers

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A store sold out because its suppliers went bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Producers' are parents, those who produce children; children become orphans when both die.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphans are children whose parents have died, so they exist because their makers are dead.

clue.text: Mangled corpse turns up in a number of stage features

indicators.note: a mangled body is torn about, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue the word in reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mutilated body appears in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mangled' rearranges CORPSE to PROSCE; 'turns up' flips IN to NI; A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Proscenia is the plural of proscenium, the arch framing a theatre stage.

clue.text: Celibate in order to be Joshua's parent

definitions.meaning: a woman vowed to chastity in a religious order
the Bible calls Joshua the son of ...

explanation.surface: A monk must stay single to become a biblical father.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a celibate sister in a religious order, and Nun is also named as Joshua's father.

clue.text: Let revolutionary remain in support

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other
revolutionary means overturned, so the letters of let are mixed

parts.note: to remain is to rest, stay put

explanation.surface: A rebel is allowed to stay in a backing role.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting framework, as for a table top.

clue.text: Plant found by the way in France

definitions.meaning: a bitter herb of the garden
the French word for street or road

explanation.surface: A flower is spotted by a French roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a bitter aromatic herb, and the French word for a street.

clue.text: Pine log used in making a bolt

indicators.note: the letters are used in making something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of pine timber is turned into a door fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like the metal fastener, but making a bolt is running off.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, and making a bolt means running away.

clue.text: Draw breath in anger over having no issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is over another piece is placed above it

parts.note: taken as written
s.p., sine prole, means without children
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone takes a breath, furious at being childless.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (Latin sine prole, 'without offspring') is used in family trees and wills.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is, in its literal sense, to breathe in or inhale.

clue.text: Astronomer put up icon to a constellation

indicators.note: one letter is put up to the top of the word

parts.note: Ali G was a cult comedy character created by Sacha Baron Cohen
Leo, the Lion, is a zodiac constellation

explanation.surface: A stargazer raises an image towards a group of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' moves the G of ALI G up to the front, giving GALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who pioneered telescopic study of the heavens.

clue.text: Collapse of society girl at Norfolk town

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering society
Acle is a small town in the Norfolk Broads, England

explanation.surface: A debutante comes to grief at a provincial town.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure or collapse.

clue.text: His disguise is in female clothes, when wielding this

definitions.text: His disguise is in female clothes, when wielding this

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man

indicators.note: disguising a word conceals it by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A man in women's clothes holds a kitchen cloth as part of his disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also pictures the user: a man in an apron at the sink, cloth in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishrag is a cloth for washing dishes, the sort of thing wielded at the sink.

clue.text: Dance with nothing on but a party decoration

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
O is zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer arrives naked except for a party trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated balloons are a standard decoration at parties.

clue.text: Chirac's boyfriend?

parts.note: Jacques Chirac, French president, would use his own language for a male friend

explanation.definitionFit: Ami is the French word for a male friend, which a French speaker such as Chirac would use.

clue.text: Charge for case used briefly by a student

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the word loses its ending

parts.note: the accusative is a grammatical case
taken as written
L is a learner, as on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: A fee for a suitcase is borrowed for a while by a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a charge laid against someone.

clue.text: Unsound property?

parts.note: not a shaky building but the quality of having no noise at all

explanation.definitionFit: Absence of sound is the defining quality of stillness and quiet.

clue.text: Wireless working, turned up for music

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces read upwards

parts.note: a wireless is an old radio set
on means switched on, working

explanation.surface: A radio is switched on and turned up to play music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like volume but reverses SETON to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes are the written symbols of music, and sheet music is sometimes called notes.

clue.text: Weariness comes over a number in European Union

annotationWithheld.why: Weariness comes over a number in European Union (5): no parse found that builds ENNUI from EU and a number; the wordplay cannot be reconstructed honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Weariness comes over a number in European Union

clue.text: Russian man of letters (55, not more)

indicators.note: the letters of the bracketed phrase are rearranged

parts.note: LV is 55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Russian writer is described with a cryptic bracketed note.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram's letters are LV (55) plus NOT MORE; the result happens to keep LV round the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Lermontov was a nineteenth-century Russian poet and novelist.

clue.text: Tour manager tries stupidly to accommodate composer with instrument

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the others in, housing them inside
acting stupidly means behaving in a muddled way, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer
an organ is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A tour manager clumsily tries to fit a composer and his instrument on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tour manager' is a surface job title and also the plain definition; 'with' simply joins the composer and the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges trips and itineraries is a tour manager or travel organiser.
